title: Four AIs fact-checked the same 42 stocks. Each missed something another caught. A case study.
author: Frodo_Baghodler
selftext:
This is a case study, not a scoreboard. One round, four models, shared context, unequal jobs. It shows what each model did with the same 42 stocks under the same written rules. It ranks nothing and predicts nothing.

Setup (15 Sep close). A script screened \~680 US stocks up more than 30% over 52 weeks: 567 passed liquidity floors, 230 passed trend filters, the top 30 by six-month momentum plus 12 sector adds made N=42. Models: GPT-6 Astra Max, Claude Fable 5.1 Max, Gemini 3.8 Flash High, Grok 4.6 X-High.

Tasks.

16 Sep, Grok: for each of the 42 — why it's up, crowding, theme, chase risk, the strongest sourced fact against it, an independent top 8.

17 Sep, Gemini: hard checks on all 42 — company-confirmed earnings date 15+ trading days out (else UNKNOWN), positive operating cash flow or 18+ months of runway, any ATM use / priced offering / convertible in the last 90 days, dated binary events, reporting currency, deal-pinned names out. Then guidance quoted against prior and consensus, revisions, insider sales, A/B/C/F grades, its own top 8.

17 Sep, Claude/Fable → Grok → Astra: audit Gemini's report against primary sources.

What the audits caught. The dilution column read "None" for names nobody had searched. TWST had priced a $300M primary offering (3.125M shares at $96) on 4 Aug. NTAP's FY27 guidance was "quoted" as $7.85–8.05B revenue and $9.50–9.70 EPS; the 8-K says $7.975–8.225B and $9.73–10.03.

What the audits missed. Reviewing a report is not doing the research. Astra redid all 42 from scratch found ABCL's \~$200M primary raise (12 Aug), CMPS's actual July at-the-market sales in its 10-Q, and HELP's \~14-month cash/burn ratio — missed by three rounds of review.

Result: 12 FAIL, 29 UNKNOWN (mostly no company-confirmed earnings date), 1 PASS-FLAG (NUE) under my entry rules. No buys cleared.

Rule change. Each model now does the whole task and saves its answer before reading any peer's. Review is a second pass, not a substitute. Every number now gets its own logged, sourced claim row.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
the dilution column reading None for names nobody searched is the whole study in one cell. an empty search and a negative result look identical in a table, so the auditor has to know which one it's looking at, and none of the models did until told. I've had the same thing with earnings dates: the model wrote a date, the date was wrong, and the wrongness was invisible because there was no source column. the fix that stuck for me was a third state for every cell, checked, unchecked, confirmed absent, and refusing to grade a row with an unchecked in it.

the part I'd want next is what happens when the top 8 goes through a written rule and gets papered, since a fact-checked list and a tradeable one are different things. I built Quantradin to run exactly that step, quantradin.com, paper only and no charge.

replies.author: Frodo_Baghodler
replies.body: Yep, you nailed it, and thanks for the suggestion!
